QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_33

question.text: In a CIV scheme, investors have rights pro-rata to their contribution in the CIV scheme's investment AND distribution of proceeds, EXCEPT:

answer.text: To the extent carried interest / additional return is shared with the Sponsor or Manager of the AIF or employees/directors/partners of the Manager of the AIF

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the 2025 SEBI CIV framework: investors of CIV scheme have rights pro-rata to contribution EXCEPT to the extent carried interest or additional return is shared with the Sponsor / Manager / employees / directors / partners of the Manager of the AIF. This preserves the carry economics but otherwise enforces pro-rata. The Trap: State VAT and SEBI fees are not exceptions contemplated. Foreign-only is fictional. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests carry treatment in CIVs. Manager's Pro-Tip: Carry on CIV deals is typically aligned with the main fund's carry (often 20% over 8% hurdle). Don't offer super-carry on CIV deals — LPs notice and it can destabilize the main-fund LP relationships.
